newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate slipped slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.55/1.50 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.48/1.43 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.63/1.58 percent against 1.56/1.51 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.55/99.65 from Monday's close of S$99.62/99.67, September 2001 at S$96.82/87 versus S$96.92/96.97 and June 2003 at S$94.83/94.93 against S$94.96/95.01.
The interbank rate slipped slightly to 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent from Monday's 3-13/16 3-11/16 percent.
